Spiritism reaches Mexico in the decades of 1850-1860
marks: The Spirits' Book is published on 18 April 1857 and Kardec coins the term spiritisme.
The Brazilian Spiritist Federation is founded here on 2 January 1884.
B. P. Hașdeu practised Spiritism at Iulia Hașdeu Castle after the loss of his daughter.
The International Spiritist Council is constituted here on 28 November 1992.
The Pan-American Spiritist Confederation has had its headquarters here since 13 October 2000.
notes: Allan Kardec publishes The Spirits' Book in France (1857) and founds the Revue Spirite (1858); by his death in 1869 the doctrine has gained 7 million followers. It reaches Mexico, Spain, Brazil and Romania, and Brazil's penal code bans its practice in 1890.
The International Spiritist Congress meets in Paris in 1925. In Brazil the code of 1940 ends the official prohibition, and the Pan-American Spiritist Confederation is founded in Argentina in 1946.
The International Spiritist Council (1992) unites national movements; in Brazil the 2010 census counts about 3.8 million Spiritists, and about 13 million are reported worldwide.
